items.title: Per-entity catalogs carry the SAME values on every entity
items.spec: Owner ruling: same catalog for all entities
items.evidence: CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS + RESOLVED on prod 2026-07-25. The 271/12/12 skew was NOT a TRK/USMCA seed gap — it was TRANSP POLLUTION: 259 of TRANSP's rows were named 'USMCA-1 leak test <hex>', written into live data by scripts/verify-no-cross-carrier-data-leak.mjs (dotenv resolved .env's prod DATABASE_DIRECT_URL; no prod refusal; committed fixtures whose DELETE cleanup threw 'permission denied' under SET ROLE ih35_app on every run and was swallowed by .catch(()=>{})). Owner soft-deactivated the 259 (is_active=false, preserved per NEVER-DELETE §F.24). Neon lucia br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a, re-verified independently by coder 2026-07-25: ACTIVE parity TRANSP 12 / TRK 12 / USMCA 12 on the identical curated list (Anonymous complaint, Civilian road complaint, Communication, Customer complaint, Driver to driver complaint, Harassment, Misconduct, Other, Retaliation, Safety Concern, Service Quality, Workplace complaint); 0 ACTIVE '%leak test%' rows; sweep of all 113 catalogs.* base tables via full-row to_jsonb ILIKE '%leak test%' found hits ONLY in complaint_types and all 259 are inactive (contained); positive control catalogs.accounts=1392 visible so the zeros are real absence, not RLS masking. NOTE the operative invariant is ACTIVE parity: TRANSP retains 259 INACTIVE archived rows that TRK/USMCA do not have, deliberately preserved for audit rather than deleted. PR #3452 (which would have seeded the garbage to all three entities) was CLOSED; the replacement ships the prod refusal + rollback-only fixtures + regression guard verify-steps/1353.

items.title: All catalogs.* carry RLS
items.evidence: SPLIT + SHARPENED 2026-07-25 (packet block 14). Neon lucia br-fancy-credit-akjnd07a: relrowsecurity=false on catalogs.account_types (15 rows) and catalogs.wo_cancellation_reasons (6). ENTITY-LEAK HALF CLEARED: neither table has an operating_company_id column, so no entity owns any row and there is nothing to leak across entities — the earlier 'RLS OFF -> cross-entity leak (P1)' framing was mis-filed. STILL FAIL on the other half: with RLS off, write authorisation on both rests entirely on the ih35_app grant, whereas the comparable global taxonomy catalogs.tire_positions restricts writes to Owner/Administrator via policy. Bringing account_types + wo_cancellation_reasons to that standard is an ADDITIVE owner-gated HELD migration, not a doc fix, so this item stays FAIL. Third table named in the original evidence, catalogs.cancellation_reasons, is the LST-F17 legacy global table being archived under ruling A (never dropped) and is tracked there, not here. Classification of all five global/shared-canonical catalogs is now recorded in docs/trackers/FINAL-TABLES-WIRING-FOR-CODER-2026-07-05.md SS A.1 and pinned to lists-module-count-spec.ts by verify-steps/1358.

items.title: Entity resolver never resolves a company the caller cannot access
items.evidence: TWO defects pulling opposite ways. M1 (latent): the default-resolution COALESCE filtered arm 2 by org.user_accessible_company_ids() but NOT arm 1, so a default outside the accessible set resolved to a non-member company - and scheduled-report-admin feeds that id into set_config('app.operating_company_id'), running the whole request's RLS under it. GRANTLESS-403 (LIVE): four non-Owner prod accounts (Administrator/Dispatcher/Manager/Safety) have a default_company_id and ZERO org.user_company_access rows, so the requested-branch membership check 403'd them for EVERY company including their own default, across 546 frontend files that pass operating_company_id. LIVE PROOF: prod simulation across all 13 accounts with a default - the 4 go old_allowed=null -> new_allowed=TRANSP (own default only), newly_denied null for all 13. ROOT CAUSE IS DATA: those 4 accounts need real grant rows (org.* = owner-gated). Guard verify-steps/1362.
